Scope of work

What we work on.

Build the provider file

Collect evidence, reconcile key details and prepare applications for provider signature. Track where each enrolment stands by payer.

Keep profiles current

Maintain CAQH documentation and re-attestation dates. A shared calendar flags licence, insurance and re-credentialing deadlines.

Follow stalled applications

The team logs payer follow-up and escalates delayed files. Contract terms and fee schedules can be summarised for review by your owner or attorney.

Deliverables

What you receive.

  • Provider document checklist and application package.
  • A shared status tracker for providers, locations and payers.
  • CAQH maintenance, re-attestation reminders and renewal calendar.

Questions

Before you start.

How long does payer enrolment take?

It varies by payer and file. Several weeks to a few months is common, and the payer controls the final decision.

Can a group practice use one tracker?

Yes. Tasks are organised by provider and payer and brought together in a shared tracker.

What is the CAQH profile used for?

Many payers use it to review provider information. Maintenance includes checking details, updating documents and tracking re-attestation dates.

Field notes

Further reading.

What is provider credentialing?

Credentialing is the review of a provider’s qualifications. A practice also needs to track payer enrollment and effective dates before it can rely on a particular network arrangement.

Credentialing checklist for a new practice

A practice preparing to see insured patients needs to coordinate provider documentation, payer applications and communication with its scheduling team.
